title: [FLINK-21321][Runtime/StateBackends] improve RocksDB incremental rescale performance by using deleteRange operator
body:
## What is the purpose of the change

Improves the performance of RocksDB state backend incremental rescales operations, where the state is being restored and clipped as part of the process. I had this change in another PR (#12345) but lacked time to clean the full changes up and add benchmarks, so this PR is now polished and benchmarked for this one focused improvement.

I created a new ticket for this at [FLINK-21321](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-21321)

This change was previously highlighted by @sihuazhou in [FLINK-8790](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-8790) and https://github.com/apache/flink/pull/5582. Previously the actual change to use `deleteRange` was not done due to it being highlighted as experimental in this comment: https://github.com/apache/flink/pull/5582#issuecomment-391574919.

`deleteRange` is in a far less experimental state now but I believe is still formally "experimental". It is heavily used  by many others like CockroachDB and TiKV and they have teased out several bugs in complex interactions over the years.

## Brief change log

- Improves performance in certain re-scale situations when using the RocksDB state backend in incremental mode.

## Verifying this change

This change is covered by existing tests, including:
* `RocksDBIncrementalCheckpointUtilsTest`
* `RocksIncrementalCheckpointRescalingTest`

And, has an added test benchmark of `RocksIncrementalCheckpointRescalingBenchmarkTest`.

I made further changes to the benchmark to generate numbers. These changes were omitted from this PR but are over in https://github.com/apache/flink/commit/3db9a8c4a1725c694bc734e99af3f2edf89f5312 on [lgo:joey-rescale-benchmark-changes](https://github.com/apache/flink/compare/master...lgo:joey-rescale-benchmark-changes). The change makes the benchmark side-by-side and run with a higher record count.

Here were the results from several test runs with that commit on my local laptop.

| Before | After | Improvement |
| ------ | ----- | ----------- |
| 2785.71ms | 2136.10ms | 23.3% |
| 2962.27ms | 2221.91ms | 24.9% |
| 2774.86ms | 2134.39ms | 23.0% |
